exposure: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (IHCP) onset timing (early-onset <=32 weeks vs. late-onset >32 weeks)
maternal serum bile acid (SBA) levels (10-19, 20-29, 30-39, >=40 micromol/L)
cohort: The study included 120 pregnant women diagnosed with Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy (IHCP) based on clinical symptoms and biochemical criteria.
finding: Late-onset IHCP and elevated maternal serum bile acid levels, particularly those >=40 micromol/L, are significantly associated with adverse maternal outcomes including higher rates of caesarean section, postpartum hemorrhage, and prolonged hospitalization.
mod_finding: Late-onset IHCP and elevated serum bile acid levels were associated with higher rates of caesarean section.
